title: "Delivery"
author: Joanne Lin

The delivery analysis explores the percentage of households in the region received packages on an average weekday

## Delivery Question

We want to know how delivery and household services contribute to travel.  

**On \<traveldate\> , which of the following occurred?**  

Select all that apply. 

- Received packages at home (e.g., USPS, FedEx, UPS) 
- Received personal packages at work if employment is not “not employed for pay”  
- Received packages at another location (e.g., Amazon locker, package pick-up point) 
- Take-out/prepared food delivered to home 
- Groceries delivered to home 
- Someone came to do work at home (e.g., babysitter, housecleaning, lawn) 
- Other item delivered to home (e.g., appliance)
- None of the above 

## Delivery Trend

- [Package delivery]{style="color:#91268F"} peaked in 2021 at 39\%. The rate stayed at about a third of regional households got packages on an average weekday.
- [Grocery + food deliveries]{style="color:#F05A28"} dramatically increased in 2021 and stayed around at 6%.
  - Grocery delivery more than doubled in 2021 and reached 5\%, but dropped to near pre-COVID level after.
  - Food delivery dramatically increased in 2021 and stayed the same since at 4\%. About 1 out of 25 households get food delivery on an average weekday
  - Grocery and food deliveries are combined for larger sample sizes
- [Service work]{style="color:#8CC63E"} was higher before the end of COVID at 6\% and dropped to about half in 2023 and 2025.
- 2\% of households have deliveries outside of home (incl. at office) in 2025. The rate is similar in 2023.

## Shopping Trip Rates

- Compared to be pre-pandemic years, the average weekday shopping rate in 2025 was almost 1/5 lower.

{{< embed /Analysis/Delivery/delivery_analysis.qmd#fig-shop-trip-rate >}}

## Delivery by Demographic Characteristics

### Household Income

- higher income households had been consistently receiving more [packages]{style="color:#91268F"} at around 40\% in 2019 and later years
- No notable difference observed in [grocery + food deliveries]{style="color:#F05A28"} by income levels

{{< embed /Analysis/Delivery/delivery_analysis.qmd#fig-package-income >}}

{{< embed /Analysis/Delivery/delivery_analysis.qmd#tbl-package-income >}}


### Vehicle Availability

- More households that owned cars had [packages]{style="color:#91268F"} delivered compare to no-car households (auto ownership may be correlated with household income)
- [Grocery + food deliveries]{style="color:#F05A28"} peaked at 8\% during COVID for household that owned vehicles, then dropped in 2023 and 2025
- [Grocery + food deliveries]{style="color:#F05A28"} for households without cars stayed high from COVID in 2021 to 2025. The service was an accessible way to get groceries and food for households without cars

:::{.panel-tabset}

### Household Composition

- in 2019 and 2025, more households with children/elders received [packages]{style="color:#91268F"} than households with adults
- No notable difference observed in [grocery + food deliveries]{style="color:#F05A28"} by household composition

{{< embed /Analysis/Delivery/delivery_analysis.qmd#fig-package-hh >}}

{{< embed /Analysis/Delivery/delivery_analysis.qmd#tbl-package-hh >}}


### Number of Workers

- In 2021 and later years, more households that had 2+ workers had  [packages]{style="color:#91268F"} delivered compare to households with fewer workers (however, number of workers may be highly correlated with household income)
- No notable difference observed in [grocery + food deliveries]{style="color:#F05A28"} by household composition

{{< embed /Analysis/Delivery/delivery_analysis.qmd#fig-package-num_workers >}}

{{< embed /Analysis/Delivery/delivery_analysis.qmd#tbl-package-num_workers >}}


### Home in Centers

- Residents in RGC generally got fewer [package deliveries]{style="color:#91268F"} than those living in other areas
- No notable trends in [grocery + food deliveries]{style="color:#F05A28"} by home in centers

{{< embed /Analysis/Delivery/delivery_analysis.qmd#fig-package-center >}}

{{< embed /Analysis/Delivery/delivery_analysis.qmd#tbl-package-center >}}


### Residence Type

- Residents in single-family/townhouse got more [package deliveries]{style="color:#91268F"} than those in apartments/condos but that gap has shrunk since the pandemic
- Decrease in [service work]{style="color:#8CC63E"} primarily attributed to decrease for single-family/townhouse, which are more likely to be owner-occupied
- No notable trends in [grocery + food deliveries]{style="color:#F05A28"} by residence type

::: {.callout-warning appearance="simple"}
Sample sizes were low for households in Apartments/Condos in 2021 and 2025
:::
